memory_candidates.content: When adding an opt-in mode flag to a hand-rolled bash+jq validator script that must coexist with existing checks, route control flow with a structural `if MODE_FLAG ... else <existing checks> fi` wrapper rather than relaxing the existing checks' jq pipelines to tolerate the new shape. This structurally prevents a 'jq error on missing key -> zero output lines -> false PASS' pattern from recurring under the new mode, and keeps the new mode's checks from ever falling through to pipelines keyed on the old required field.

A jq pipeline like `.key[]` over a JSON object missing `key` raises a runtime error ('Cannot iterate over null') and exits nonzero. If the caller captures that pipeline's output via `$(... 2>/dev/null)` and then checks only 'is the captured string empty' to decide PASS/FAIL, a missing key silently becomes a false PASS -- the error is swallowed by stderr redirection and the empty-output heuristic can't distinguish 'checked, found nothing' from 'could not check at all'. When auditing a validator script for this class of bug, don't trust the research-report's count of VISIBLE jq-error lines in sample output -- checks that already redirect stderr to /dev/null will false-PASS silently with no visible error line at all, so the true affected-check count is usually higher than what a quick manual run surfaces.

When a task's plan instructs grepping the writer set for additional real-world shapes beyond what research named ('in case a fourth insert site exists that the research pass did not reach'), take that instruction literally even when research already named a plausible-sounding exact count -- in one case a grep for a 'third' documented writer shape surfaced two more real, already-firing writer shapes, one of which exposed a genuine allowlist gap that needed a code fix, not just a new test fixture.
